title: Grade 8 Science — Fri, Jun 27
description: Force and Pressure — Day 5 of 5: Full mixed review
subject: science

questions.question: Force is a push or pull. Its SI unit is:
questions.explanation: Force SI unit = Newton (N). 1 N = force to accelerate 1 kg by 1 m/s². Pressure SI unit = Pascal (Pa). Energy/work = Joule (J). Power = Watt (W). Named after Isaac Newton.

questions.question: Pressure formula is P = F/A. A force of 60 N acts on 3 m². Pressure =
Which type of friction is least: static, kinetic, or rolling?
questions.explanation: Order (highest to lowest): static > kinetic (sliding) > rolling. Rolling friction is the smallest — that's why wheels were invented. Ball bearings in machines use rolling friction to replace sliding friction, reducing energy waste.

questions.question: Archimedes' principle: upthrust = weight of fluid ___.
questions.explanation: Archimedes: upthrust = weight of fluid displaced by the object. Not the surrounding fluid — only the fluid whose volume equals the submerged part of the object. If you submerge 500 cm³ of an object in water: upthrust = weight of 500 cm³ of water = 5 N.

questions.question: A magnet attracting a nail is an example of which type of force?
questions.explanation: Magnetic force = non-contact force. No physical contact needed between magnet and nail. Other non-contact forces: gravity, electrostatic. Contact forces: friction, normal, tension, muscular, applied force.

questions.question: A knife cuts better when sharp because:
options: P = F/A — smaller edge area → greater pressure for same force → penetrates material
questions.explanation: P = F/A. Sharp edge: very small area → huge pressure → cuts easily. Same force, less area = more pressure. Needles, drawing pins, blades all use this principle. Blunt knife: same force, larger area → less pressure → harder to cut.

questions.question: Lubrication reduces friction by:
options: Creating a fluid film between surfaces — surfaces glide on fluid (much less than solid-surface friction)
questions.explanation: Lubricants (oil, grease): thin fluid layer between surfaces → surfaces don't touch directly → fluid friction replaces solid friction (fluid friction << solid friction). Applied to: engine oil, bicycle chain grease, door hinge oil, machine bearings.

questions.question: A ship floats in the ocean. The buoyant force on the ship equals:
options: Volume of sea water in the ocean
Weight of sea water displaced by the ship (equal to ship's weight for floating)
Pressure at the bottom of the ship
questions.explanation: Floating condition: buoyant force = weight of ship. Buoyant force = weight of displaced sea water. So: weight of displaced sea water = weight of ship. The ship displaces just enough sea water (equal weight) to stay afloat. Archimedes' principle in practice.

questions.question: Why are mountaineers advised to carry supplemental oxygen above 5,000 m?
options: Air becomes toxic at high altitude
Atmospheric pressure decreases with altitude → fewer oxygen molecules per breath → breathing becomes difficult
Oxygen is used to make fire at high altitude
questions.explanation: Atmospheric pressure decreases with altitude (less air above). Lower pressure → lower oxygen partial pressure → fewer O₂ molecules in each breath → blood carries less oxygen → hypoxia. At Everest (~8,849 m), atmospheric pressure is ~1/3 of sea-level pressure. Supplemental O₂ compensates.

questions.question: Net force on a book resting on a table =
options: Zero — weight (down) and normal force (up) are equal and opposite → balanced forces
questions.explanation: Book at rest on table: Weight W = mg acts downward. Normal force N = mg acts upward. Net force = W−N = 0. Balanced forces → no acceleration → remains at rest (Newton's 1st law). Friction is zero because the book is not moving or attempting to move horizontally.

questions.question: Hydraulic press (Pascal's Law): small piston area = 5 cm², large piston area = 500 cm². Force applied on small piston = 100 N. Force on large piston =
questions.explanation: Pascal's Law: P₁ = P₂ → F₁/A₁ = F₂/A₂ → F₂ = F₁×A₂/A₁ = 100×500/5 = 100×100 = 10,000 N. This is mechanical advantage of 100×. The hydraulic press multiplies force by area ratio. Used in car jacks, presses, brakes.

questions.question: An iceberg floats with ~90% submerged. This means:
options: Ice is 90% as dense as water
Ice density ≈ 0.9 g/cm³, water = 1.0 g/cm³; fraction submerged = ice density/water density = 0.9 → 90% below water
Salt water pushes ice down more
questions.explanation: Fraction submerged = density of object/density of fluid. Ice density ≈ 0.917 g/cm³, water = 1.0 → 91.7% submerged. This is why icebergs are dangerous — most mass is hidden below the waterline. The Titanic struck an iceberg's underwater portion. Direct application of buoyancy and density.

questions.question: Friction converts kinetic energy to heat. Evidence of this in everyday life:
options: Hands rubbing together become warm; fire made by rubbing sticks; brake discs heating when car stops; tyres warming during driving
questions.explanation: Friction → heat: (1) Rub hands together → warm. (2) Rubbing sticks → fire (ancient method). (3) Car brakes → disc and pad heat up (sometimes glow red in emergency braking). (4) Tyre friction with road → tyres warm (hot on long drives). Energy is conserved — kinetic → thermal.

questions.question:
Three devices and their forces — match each device to the type of force it uses:
(A) Hydraulic brake (B) Electromagnet crane (C) Suction cup
questions.explanation: A: Hydraulic brake = fluid pressure transmitted by Pascal's Law. B: Electromagnet crane = electromagnetic force (non-contact — magnets attract iron without touching). C: Suction cup = atmospheric pressure — when you press, air is expelled; atmospheric pressure outside holds cup against surface. B ✓.

questions.question: Summary: P = F/A. Both P = F/A and Archimedes' principle depend on the concept of ___; friction depends on ___; buoyancy in a balloon depends on ___.
options: Force per area / surface roughness and normal force / density difference between balloon gas and surrounding air
questions.explanation: P = F/A: pressure = force per unit area. Friction: depends on normal force (weight pressing down) and surface roughness (coefficient of friction). Hot air balloon buoyancy: hot air inside less dense than outside cool air → upthrust > weight → rises. Three pillars of this week: force, pressure (F/A), friction (surface), buoyancy (density/Archimedes).
